chapter: War years, Decca records and La Conga
title: Jack Robbins and the coast-to-coast midnight broadcasts
summary: Publisher Jack Robbins arranged radio time from La Conga to plug the music he published; few air checks survive.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Okay. Macho, the - ahh - when did you first learn about the midnight broadcast from coast to coast? Was that something that you and Mario asked for or did that come by accident?
Well, Jack Robbins in account that he had the publishing house, all the publishing house was helping the radio station.....
WOR? MUTUAL
WOR, NBC, whatever, the station was providing the music. The publishing that was helping us to get off

the line like Noro Morales and myself and Le Baron, all those guys, you understand, because the publishing company want us to play the number that was published so it was a combination in order to expose what they published.
I see, so then it was Robbins that, that set this up with La Conga?
Uh Huh
So, who, who payed for the expenses?
La Conga.
And Robbins?
And Robbins, and ......
Okay, so some of the things that we heard live - "El Bombero Arrollador", ah - "Nague", "Rumba Suite Tango", you know, all of these things. You mean to say Robbins was the publisher of all the .....
Yes
....everything that he did then, ah?
Everything.
Ahh, that's a brilliant idea. I had no idea why that was done. (End of tape reel I) / Macho, do you remember the year that you first broadcasted from La Conga Club?
It was in 1942.
Nineteen forty-two? As early as that?
Yes.
Ahh, okay. I noticed that the things that you showed me, the things that you had, the earliest one was 1945 and the other ones after that was '46. They didn't make no air checks then - out of '42?
I don't remember. Maybe not because we were the ones to make those copies. I used to be uhh - we were so happy about where we are going that we didn't make no copy out of it.
I see. Even though Robbins Music owned the rights to the publishing rights, they didn't make no copies of those air checks?
No because they had the - the - from the ASCAP or from the BMI or whatever, they notified the broadcaster.
